newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Six rebels, one soldier dead in Colombia fighting.
newsitem.headline: Six rebels, one soldier dead in Colombia fighting.

text.p: Clashes between the army and leftist guerrillas in southern Colombia on Wednesday left six rebels and one soldier dead, a regional army commander said.

The firefights took place a short distance from the town of Cartagena del Chaira, in Caqueta province, where the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) released 70 soldiers, some of whom they had held prisoner for more than nine months, in a public ceremony on June 15.

Gen. Gabriel Contreras, head of the army's 12th brigade based in regional capital Florencia, said all the dead rebels were members of the FARC's 14th Front -- led by Fabian Ramirez, one of the rebel commanders who played a key role in the handover of the captured soldiers last month.

It was the second major violent outbreak in the province since the captive troops were freed. Late last month the FARC killed five soldiers when they ambushed a military patrol as it was checking boats passing up and down one of the main rivers that cuts through the zone.
Contreras told reporters that fighting in the area around Cartagena del Chaira had been going on for two days and said operations to hunt down the FARC column were continuing.
